title: Warp-hole UX — user still re-enters teleports with continuous movement after fix #184
summary: User report after fix #184 (per-entity stamp): 'I don't like how teleports work — I appear from a random side and if I continue movement I get into a teleport again. I think teleport should not fire if you teleported into it but haven't gone outside.' The proposed behaviour is exactly what #184 implements at the SPECIFIC destination cell, but the user is still hitting re-warp during continuous motion. Two plausible gaps: (a) destination B is adjacent to ANOTHER warp pair's cell — user emerges at B holding ArrowRight, walks one cell off B (recentlyWarpedTo cleared), lands on a different warp, teleports again; (b) after stepping off destination, the user immediately steps back onto the SAME destination cell (recentlyWarpedTo was cleared the moment they left) — re-warps. The warpfield arena has 3 pairs / 6 cells and they can be close to each other; the user's continuous-input experience is plausibly correct. Fix #184's per-entity stamp is the right primitive but the granularity (clears on the first cell-change) is too short to feel calm in moment-to-moment play.
repro: Walk player.1 into any warp cell using continuous ArrowRight (or another direction) — don't tap, hold.
After teleport, KEEP holding the direction key. Don't pause.

Observed: bomber emerges at destination B, walks off B to a neighbour, and if the next cell along the same direction is another warp cell, teleports again. Visually 'bounces' through teleport events without the user releasing the key.

Note: my Playwright tests for this case were unreliable because force-writing `GridPosition` doesn't trigger the grid-occupancy spatial index, and `kaboom.gotoCell` crashed with `Cannot set component "AgentGoto" on missing entity "2"` (a separate bug worth its own ticket). The repro above relies on live keyboard input.
expected: Stronger UX rule: after teleporting, give the entity a brief grace window (~0.5 s, ≈ 2 grid steps at speed=4) during which NO warp on ANY cell fires for that entity. Alternative: 'pass-through' design — the warp cell delivers the entity to the cell ADJACENT to the destination in the direction they were walking, never standing on the destination warp itself. Many Bomberman-likes do this — the warp is a doorway, not a stopping point.
actual: Per-entity `recentlyWarpedTo` stamp clears the instant the entity's GridPosition stops matching the destination cell. With continuous input (key held) at speed=4 = 250 ms per cell, the entity is OFF the destination cell within one grid-mover tick — stamp cleared — eligible for re-warp the next step. If the user's path crosses any other warp cell (or comes back to the original destination), they teleport again.
